key_insight: A simple history-aware classical model outperformed all tested LLM variants for next dental procedure prediction, while the proposed DentaCoPilot added calibrated uncertainty, abstention, and chart-grounded rationale.
clinical_relevance: This work suggests decision support for dentistry may be more reliable when it combines prior procedure history with calibrated selective prediction rather than relying on zero-shot LLMs alone.
method: Compared 4 classical baselines and 6 LLM variants for next-procedure recommendation.
Built DentaCoPilot to output top-K CDT codes, confidence labels, an abstain flag, and a rationale.
Used split-conformal prediction to support selective prediction with coverage guarantees.
evidence_signal: On MEPS 2023 data (11,016 next-visit transitions from 5,088 patients), the history-aware model reached 0.479 top-1 accuracy versus 0.297 for a most-frequent baseline and had ECE 0.031; in synthetic tests, classical baselines reached 0.567 top-1 while pure LLMs ranged from 0.267 to 0.467.
watch_item: The synthetic evaluation reflects pipeline behavior rather than externally valid clinical performance, and CDT-level real-world validation plus clinician-in-the-loop testing are still needed.
paper_title: A Zero-Shot Decision Model (Jev) Matches a Trained Classifier but Ranks Its Own Errors Worse: Calibrated, Split-Conformal Next-Procedure Recommendation in General Dentistry
